_comment: Source of truth for tools/build.py (metadata, levels, conversion options). schemaVersion 2 (L1 plan, docs/superpowers/plans/2026-10-14-l1-curated-library.md).

Pieces: this file's 'pieces' (the core 30, in their original order), then the 'pieces' of every tools/catalog.d/*.json fragment in file-name order. A fragment is {"task": ..., "pieces": [...], "rejected": [...]}, one per implementer; slugs are unique across all of them.

collections: the controlled vocabulary [{id, title, kind: 'set' | 'genre'}] in display order. Each piece names one collection id; the manifest gets both 'collection' (the title) and 'collectionId'. manifest.json and verification.json are ordered by (level, collection display order, position in the merged catalog).
Levels: 1 first steps (five-finger position), 2 easy (ABRSM ~1-2), 3 moderate (~2-4), 4 intermediate (~5-6), 5 challenging (~6-7); 6 advanced arrives with L2.

Every piece: slug; source ('own' or 'mutopia'); level; title; composer; composerDates; catalogue; year; tempoBpm (quarter notes per minute, the same unit as MusicXML <sound tempo>); tempoSource (where the tempo comes from: a printed mark, the source's \midi block, or 'editorial: ...' with the reason); collection (an id from 'collections'); levelNote (one line: the syllabus placement and the level heuristic's proposal); levelOverride (only when the final level differs from the heuristic's proposal by more than one: the reason); benchmarkSet ('core30' on the first 30 pieces; omitted, meaning null, on every later piece); notes.

Mutopia pieces: ftpDir (the directory fetch_mutopia.py downloads); main (the RDF lyFile); subdir (when the main file sits in a sub-folder); publishedMidi; retrievedAt (pinned YYYY-MM-DD: it becomes <encoding-date> and source.retrievedAt, so a re-fetch does not move a byte); sourceSha256 (SHA-256 of the fetched main .ly); convert ({score: the n-th \score, barFrom, barTo, staffOrder, patches, textReplace, dropText, minFingerings}); excerpt (what part of the piece is kept, when not all of it); keyName (the musical key, where the key signature alone misnames it); compactXml (optional true: remove intertag XML indentation without changing musical text or attributes).

Own arrangements (generated by arrange.py): arranger ('digitus2 project'); melody ({authors: [{name, died}] or 'traditional', firstPublished: year or null, reference: {url, retrieved, description}}). Rule for new arrangements: every melody author died in 1955 or earlier and the melody was first published in 1928 or earlier (public domain in the US and the EU).
Fragment pieces may also carry addedBy ('Task N', with the reason) for a replacement candidate taken from the mirror.

genres: the controlled vocabulary [{id, title}] in display order (UI batch, docs/superpowers/specs/2026-10-14-ui-batch-design.md section 4.2). Every collection names one genre id ('genre'); a piece may carry 'genre' to override its collection's (Für Elise is 'classical'); the manifest gets 'genre' (the id) after 'collectionId'. A collection's 'kind' is unrelated: it says whether its title names a kind of music or a published set.

pieces.tempoSource: set by the M0 content agent (docs/research/content-library.md)
pieces.notes: Right hand in C position (the A is a small stretch of the 5th finger); left hand plays whole-note and half-note C-position chords.

pieces.notes: Melody in the right hand around C position (the A4 in bars 5-6 and the low G3 of the closing ding-dang-dong need small extensions); left hand alternates C and G.

pieces.tempoSource: set by the M0 content agent (docs/research/content-library.md)

pieces.title: Happy Birthday to You
pieces.composer: Mildred J. Hill and Patty Hill
pieces.tempoSource: set by the M0 content agent (docs/research/content-library.md)
pieces.notes: In the public domain in the United States since the 2016 settlement of Marya v. Warner/Chappell (the court found no valid copyright in the lyrics, 2015); in the EU the song entered the public domain on 1 January 2017. Melody spans an octave, so it needs one hand shift.

pieces.notes: Traditional Dorian melody with an open-fifth accompaniment; deliberately avoids the copyrighted 1966 Simon & Garfunkel arrangement and its 'Canticle' counter-melody.

pieces.tempoSource: set by the M0 content agent (docs/research/content-library.md)
pieces.notes: Easy arrangement in augmentation (half notes, as in most easy editions): the left hand plays the famous eight-note ground bass, the right hand the first two lines of the first violin, which move in 3rds and 5ths against the bass.
